title: Words & Alphabets
goal: Work with alphabets, words and λ, count `Σᵏ`, `Σ≤ⁿ`, combine languages with set operations, and check strings against a grammar.
magic: Σ: finite, non-empty. Words: finite strings. `λ`: length 0, vanishes in concatenation.
A language is any subset of `Σ*`.
Grammars: compulsory parts first; `( … )*` may be empty.

blocks.title: 💡 Learn it, one idea at a time
Alphabets, words and the empty word λ
blocks.summary: An alphabet Σ is a finite, non-empty set of symbols. A word is a finite string of them. λ is the word with no symbols.
blocks.picture: Σ is the keys on a keyboard. A word is anything you can type with them: a password, a variable name, even "nothing yet" (the empty text box, λ).
blocks.official: `Σ`: an **alphabet**, a finite, nonempty set (Week 1, slide 42), e.g. `{a, …, z}`, `{0, 1}`, `{0, …, 9}`, or all Chinese characters (no ordering needed). A **word** is any finite string of symbols from Σ; the **empty word** is `λ` (slide 43). `length(ω)` = number of symbols: `length(aaa) = 3`, `length(λ) = 0`. The only operation is **concatenation**, written by juxtaposition: `νω`. `λω = ω = ωλ`; `length(νω) = length(ν) + length(ω)`.

tries.q: Is `λ` a symbol of the alphabet?
tries.a: **No.** It's a word (of length 0), not a symbol.
tries.why: Σ contains symbols; words are strings built from them.

trap.correct: `λ` is the **empty** word: no characters at all. A space would be a symbol of length 1 (and only if it's in Σ).

blocks.magic: Σ finite and non-empty; words finite; `λ` has length 0 and vanishes in concatenation.

blocks.title: `Σᵏ`, `Σ*`, `Σ⁺` and `Σ≤ⁿ`
blocks.summary: `Σᵏ` = words of length k (`|Σ|ᵏ` of them). `Σ*` = all words (infinite). `Σ⁺` = all except λ. `Σ≤ⁿ` = lengths 0 to n.
blocks.picture: A 4-digit PIN comes from `{0, …, 9}⁴`: `10⁴ = 10 000` PINs. "Any PIN of any length" is `{0, …, 9}*`, which never ends.
blocks.official: Notation (Week 1, slide 44): `Σᵏ` = set of all words of length `k`; `Σ⁰ = {λ}`, `Σ¹ = Σ`. `Σ* = Σ⁰ ∪ Σ¹ ∪ Σ² ∪ …` (all words). `Σ⁺ = Σ¹ ∪ Σ² ∪ … = Σ* \ {λ}` (nonempty words). `Σ≤ⁿ = ⋃ᵢ₌₀ⁿ Σⁱ`. Counting: `|Σᵏ| = |Σ|ᵏ`; lecture example (slide 45): for `Σ = {a, b, c}`, `|Σ*| = ∞` and `|Σ≤⁴| = 3⁰ + 3¹ + … + 3⁴ = (3⁵ − 1)/2 = 121`.

steps: `Σ²`: every 2-letter word: `xx, xy, xz, yx, yy, yz, zx, zy, zz` (`3² = 9`).

tries.why: `Σ⁺` excludes λ, so only the one-letter words remain (that's `Σ¹ = Σ`).

check.expr: sorted(w for w in upto({'x','y','z'}, 1) if w != '')

tries.q: Is `Σ*` finite for some alphabet Σ?
tries.why: Σ is non-empty, so words of every length exist: `a, aa, aaa, …`

trap.test: Ask: is the empty word allowed? `*` yes, `+` no.

blocks.magic: `|Σᵏ| = |Σ|ᵏ`. `*` includes λ, `+` doesn't. `|Σ≤ⁿ|` = a geometric sum.

blocks.title: A language is any set of words
blocks.summary: Any subset of `Σ*` is a language, so languages can be combined with `∪ ∩ \`.
blocks.picture: "Valid email addresses" is a language over the keyboard alphabet: some strings are in, most aren't. "Valid AND under 20 characters" is an intersection of two languages.
blocks.official: A **language** is a subset of `Σ*` (Week 1, slide 44). Typically we care about subsets described by rules; such a collection of rules is a **grammar** (programming languages, database query languages). Since languages are sets, all set operations apply, e.g. `Σ² ∩ Ψ²`, `Σ* ∪ Ψ*`.

tries.q: Same Σ, Ψ. Is `Σ* ∩ Ψ* = (Σ ∩ Ψ)*`?
tries.why: A word uses only symbols from Σ **and** only symbols from Ψ exactly when it uses only symbols from `Σ ∩ Ψ`.

tries.q: Same Σ, Ψ. Is `Σ* ∪ Ψ* = (Σ ∪ Ψ)*`?
tries.a: **No.** `ac ∈ (Σ ∪ Ψ)*`, but `ac` is in neither `Σ*` nor `Ψ*`.
tries.why: Mixing symbols from both alphabets is allowed on the right only.

check.expr: 'ac' in upto({'a','b','c'}, 2) and 'ac' not in upto({'a','b'}, 2) and 'ac' not in upto({'b','c'}, 2)

tries.q: `Σ = {0, 1}`. List `{ω ∈ Σ³ : ω contains at most one 1}`.
tries.why: Zero 1s: one word. One 1: three positions.

check.expr: sorted(w for w in words({'0','1'}, 3) if w.count('1') <= 1)

tries.q: Is `∅` a language over Σ? Is `{λ}`?
tries.a: **Both are**, and they're different: `∅` has no words, `{λ}` has one (the empty word).
tries.why: Any subset of `Σ*` counts, including these two.

trap.correct: `∅` contains **no** words; `{λ}` contains **one** word, the empty one.

blocks.magic: Language = any subset of `Σ*`; use set operations on it.

blocks.title: Grammars: rules that describe a language
blocks.summary: A grammar lists which symbols may come first, next and how often, like a regex. `(…)*` means "zero or more times".
blocks.picture: The rules for a UNSW zID: the letter `z`, then exactly 7 digits. `z1234567` fits; `Z1234567` and `z123456` don't.
blocks.official: A grammar is a collection of descriptive/formative rules for a language (Week 1, slide 44). In the notation of Problem set 2, Q2(b): `|` means "or", `( … )*` means "repeat zero or more times", and quoted symbols are literal. The same language can be written as a set: e.g. `{νω : ν ∈ 𝓛, ω ∈ (𝓛 ∪ 𝓓)*}`.

watch.q: A topic-name grammar: `topic ::= letter (letter | digit | "." | "_" | "-")*`, where `letter ::= "a" | … | "z"` and `digit ::= "0" | … | "9"`. Which are valid: `orders.v2`, `2orders`, `user_events-dlq`, `Orders`?
steps: `orders.v2`: starts with a letter; the rest are letters, a dot and a digit ✅.
`2orders`: the first symbol must be a letter ❌.

tries.q: Same grammar. Is the one-letter word `a` valid? Is the empty word λ?
tries.why: `( … )*` allows zero repeats, but the first `letter` is compulsory.

tries.q: Write the topic language as a set, with `𝓛 = {a, …, z}` and `𝓓 = {0, …, 9}`.
tries.why: One compulsory first letter `ν`, then any word `ω` over the allowed symbols.

tries.q: A zID is `"z" digit digit digit digit digit digit digit`. How many different zIDs are possible?
tries.why: The `z` is fixed; 7 digit positions with 10 choices each: `10⁷`.

trap.correct: `*` means **zero** or more. ("One or more" would be written with `⁺`.)
trap.test: Check whether the shortest possible word stops right before the starred part.

blocks.magic: Follow the rule symbol by symbol: compulsory parts first, `*` parts can be empty.

items.why: Remove the words made only of `b` and `c`: only `bb` goes.

items.q: Topic grammar from Idea 4: valid or not? `a-`, `a..b`, `_x`.
items.why: After the first letter, any mix of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` is allowed, even repeated dots. But `_` can't come first.

blocks.sub: Problem set 2, Q1(a) and Q2 style: words of bounded length, language operations, and a grammar. Original alphabets and grammar.

items.q: A config-key grammar: `key ::= letter (letter | "_")* ("." letter (letter | "_")*)*` with `letter ::= "a" | … | "z"`. Which are valid?
items.why: (1) one segment. (2) can't start with `.`. (3) two segments. (4) `.` must be followed by a letter, so it can't end a key. (5) underscores are fine after the first letter. (6) `_` can't start a segment.
Keep the 2-letter words over Σ that use at least one `c`.

items.q: `Σ = {x, y}`. List every element of `{ω ∈ Σ* : length(ω) ≤ 2 and ω doesn't start with y}`.
items.why: λ has no first letter, so it doesn't start with `y`: it's in.

check.expr: sorted(w for w in upto({'x','y'}, 2) if not w.startswith('y'))

items.q: True or false: for all alphabets Σ, Ψ, `(Σ ∩ Ψ)* ⊆ Σ*`.
items.why: A word using only common symbols uses only symbols of Σ.

items.q: `Σ = {a, b}`. How many words of length 6 contain **no** two `b`s next to each other?
items.why: Count by the last letter: it's the Fibonacci pattern `f(n) = f(n − 1) + f(n − 2)`, with `f(1) = 2`, `f(2) = 3`: 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, **21**.

check.expr: sum(1 for w in words({'a','b'}, 6) if 'bb' not in w)

items.why: Concatenating any number (including zero, giving λ) of non-empty words gives every word, and nothing else.
Each extra length multiplies by 26; all shorter lengths together are only about 1/25 of the next level.

items.q: For which alphabets is `Σ* \ Σ⁺` not equal to `{λ}`?

lines: Alphabet Σ, words, λ, length, concatenation (not commutative).
Languages are sets: `Σ* ∩ Ψ* = (Σ ∩ Ψ)*`, but `Σ* ∪ Ψ* ≠ (Σ ∪ Ψ)*` in general.
